newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Banks bailout drags Australian stocks down at open.
newsitem.headline: Banks bailout drags Australian stocks down at open.

text.p: The Australian share market continued its downward trend at the open on Friday as traders bailed out of the big banks after Wall Street weakened and as local bonds dipped.
The All Ordinaries index lost 13.6 points to 2,462.7.
Modest losses were present in most of the leaders but banks were the worst hit. Golds bucked the trend, the gold index jumping over one percent after the bullion price strengthened.
"Banks are where the losses are," said a dealer at a Sydney-based brokerage.
"They struck some profit-taking yesterday and with bonds off they have hit some selling again," he said, noting the focus on the banks with the other leaders narrowly weaker.
"For the rest, there is not much in it and (the market) is already off the bottom."
On the upside, golds impressed with the sector index showing a rise of 1.2 percent after the bullion price jumped overnight.
Acacia Resources, up five to A$2.31 (US$1.79), and Emperor Mines, up 12 to A$2.45, were the pick.
Qantas Airways continued to fly high after Thursday's first half net profit of A$151.6 million. Its shares climbed six cents to A$2.52, their highest altitude ever.
Falls outnumbered rises by a ratio of about eight to five, while about 38 percent of stock traded remained steady.
